scope: Native functional qtest source; no execution result or silicon/cache timing claim.

profiles.positive: -M esp32s3 -m 8M -S; real SPI1 CS1 ssi_psram, exactly 8388608 backed bytes. Cache consumers first issue SPI1 35 in chip SPI mode, then program real SPI0 phases. Pure SPI1 transport/identity consumers start in uninitialized SPI mode.
profiles.absent: -M esp32s3 -m 0 -S; absent chip must raise GDMA descriptor errors
profiles.other_capacities: Unsupported nonzero sizes and octal properties must fail realize under SSI contract; this suite does not qualify other SKUs or startup-error subprocess behavior.
profiles.flash_xts: No flash drive attached and no flash/XTS qualification inferred. Existing boot-profile execution is separately owned.

prerequisites: Memory copies integrated into native QEMU, including cache CPU I/O target and separate MMU-translating GDMA I/O target
Machine soc_mr owns internal DRAM alias at 0x3fc80000 and cache.psram_dma at 0x3c000000
Frozen GDMA artifacts retained: MEMTX_DECODE_ERROR becomes DSCR_ERR
Parent SPI1 transport patch compares transfer index rather than byte value in both TX/RX bounds
SSI child data_mr is the sole physical PSRAM array
SPI0 at 0x60003000 reuses official ESP32S3SpiState with cache-port=true and validates actual cache phases against the sole SPI1 CS1 chip; no second SSI backing
esp32s3_spi_psram_cache_ready(spi0, psram, write) gates physical CPU cache misses/writeback and direct GDMA read/write; cached CPU hits do not require external traffic
EXT sync size zero and address zero implement whole-cache ROM convention

fixtures.mmu: 512 shared entries, 64KiB pages; type bit15 PSRAM, invalid bit14, physical page bits0..13
fixtures.dcache: CTRL enable|8 selects 32-byte lines, 32KiB; CTRL1=0 opens CPU buses. Four ways; bit1 reserved and left clear.
fixtures.maintenance: EXT 0x28: invalidate=1, writeback=2, clean=4, done=8; address0x2c, block count0x30
fixtures.writeback_fault: Same pinned extmem_reg.h: illegal status0xe4 DCACHE_SYNC_OP_FAULT bit2, W1C at0xe0 bit2. Write-invalid vectors first clear/assert0, require fault status plus retained cached bytes after failed WB, clear/assert0, restore actualSPI0 phases and retry: known committed bytes change only after successful retry and fault status stays0. SYNC_DONE means command completion, not successful data commitment.
fixtures.spi01_system: Same IDF primary pin, soc/esp32s3/register/soc/reg_base.h and system_reg.h: SYSTEM0x600c0000, PERIP_CLK_EN0 offset0x18 and PERIP_RST_EN0 offset0x20 share SPI01 bit1. Gate cycling preserves phases/storage; held reset prevents physical access and ignores SPI0 phase writes; release requires fresh programming. Controller-only reset preserves externalQPI/data and CPUcache/MMU/dirtybytes.
fixtures.cpu_access: qtest accesses system address-space data alias MemoryRegion; not execution of Xtensa cache instructions
fixtures.gdma_access: Raw MMIO M2M internal descriptors; never external descriptor placement. GDMA sees committed SSI storage, not dirty CPU lines.

spi0.cache_sctrl_0x40: 0x0055c174: QIO bit2, read dummy enable bit4, user read bit5/write bit20, address23<<14, read dummy5<<6; reset write-dummy length1<<22 retained but write-dummy enable bit3 clear
spi0.read_command_0x48: 0x700000eb: eight command bits, EB QPI read
spi0.sram_clock_0x50: 0x00010001: N=1,H=0,L=1; core selector0 at0xec and register gate1 at0xe8, qualified80MHz/2 configuration
spi0.smem_ddr_0xe4: 0x00003020 reset mask/minimum-byte fields retained; DDR enable bit0 clear
spi0.chip_mode: Real SSI35 transitions chip SPI to QPI; SPI1 FCMD_QUAD bit8 selected for subsequent QPI commands. Reconfigure SPI0 only after warm reset; do not reissue35 while chip is already QPI.
spi0.negative_observation: Valid MMU/backing plus invalid selected phase returns native OUT_DSCR_ERR bit2 or IN_DSCR_ERR bit3, preserves destination guard/committed SSI bytes, and resumes known byte transport after actual-register restoration. Incorrect read-only phases do not suppress valid writes; incorrect write-only phases do not suppress valid reads.

fixtures.pio: SPI1 USR, CS0 disabled and CS1 enabled; FIFO transfers <=64 bytes. Eight32-byte transactions cover all256 byte values. Simultaneous SPI READ MOSI/MISO with all FIFO bytes>=0x80 uses TX32/RX32 and TX2/RX32; both must return the same known SSI source bytes, not stale clock bytes. These consumer assertions distinguish the original byte-value transport bounds from corrected index bounds.
